From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Tom Nguyen <tnguyen@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC follow-up: access steps & success criteria

Hi Lisa / Tom,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — really appreciate the time. I wanted to recap the proposed POC scope and next steps so we have alignment on success criteria and what we need from your side to get access provisioned.

Summary of proposed POC (what we discussed):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for ACME search assistant across customer support KB (latency and quality).
- Duration: 3 weeks (pilot) with a 1-week internal soak.
- Success criteria (high level):
  - 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms for 512-token requests under pilot load
  - Top-1 answer accuracy >= 82% on the evaluation prompt set you shared
  - Average cost per 1k tokens meets target (TBD after initial run)

What we need from ACME to start provisioning:
1) API access: preferred routing — do you want a dedicated API key for the POC or a scoped service account?
2) Network: list of outbound IP ranges to allow (we will need to be added to your IP allowlist for callback testing).
3) SSO invites: please add marissa@redwood.com and rafael@redwood.com to your SCIM/Okta group for the pilot user role.
4) Dataset access: a sanitized subset of the KB (S3 link or Google Drive) and the evaluation prompt set you mentioned.

Proposed timeline:
- Fri 10/2: ACME provides network contact + preferred service account email and the KB sample
- Mon 10/5: Redwood provisions sandbox instance, issues API key, and sends SSO invites
- Week of 10/5: Integration support + initial smoke tests

If that looks right, can you confirm the network contact and whether you want a dedicated API key vs a scoped service account? I can loop in our infra lead (Neha) to handle IP allowlist and keys.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
